commits.message:
[marina] Rebuild applets before publishing (#8927)

Run a declared applet `build_command` before every normal publish,
including when `dist/index.html` already exists. `--no-build` remains
the explicit path for reusing a prebuilt bundle, so normal publishes do
not silently reuse stale Vue or Vite output.

Document Vue and Vite applets in the Marina README and `marina-applet`
skill. The guidance uses Vite `base: "./"`, Vue Router
`createWebHashHistory()`, and relative backend calls so one `dist/`
works below both current and revision URLs. JavaScript dependencies must
be bundled because the applet policy sets `script-src 'self'`.

---------

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Remove object hashing and prune unfiltered limits (#8923)

Stop SHA-256 verification and content-derived naming in Finelog's object
persistence path. Cache hits perform metadata I/O only, downloads check
byte length, remote pointer swaps use the provider version or ETag, and
local pointer swaps compare exact bytes under the file lock. Immutable
objects receive UUID names. Migration checkpoints use immutable catalog
metadata without reading source files. The removed protobuf field number
remains reserved, and readers ignore the field in older JSON catalogs.

An unfiltered `LIMIT` pushed to a table scan now uses catalog row counts
to present the smallest segment prefix that can satisfy the request.
Filters, absent limits, and missing row counts retain all candidate
segments.

On `bento-cat`, a debug build read one copied 30.5 MB production
`levanter.metrics` L3 shard through 402 local hardlinks. Cache lookup
fell from 337.881 seconds to 9 milliseconds. The pre-change `perf
record` profile spent over 90% of samples in the SHA-256 pipeline; the
new profile contains no SHA frames. The first `SELECT * FROM
"levanter.metrics" LIMIT 100` fell from 142 to 73 milliseconds, and 150
post-change runs had a 51.81 millisecond median. Fourteen
training-dashboard queries were also measured over 15-minute and default
three-hour windows. Ordinary-panel medians were 35.08 to 63.36
milliseconds and 35.48 to 61.77 milliseconds; execution health took
110.29 and 132.34 milliseconds. Remaining CPU for the wide limit query
is dominated by Zstandard decompression. The benchmark and operational
record is at https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/338.

Follow-up to #8917 and #8909.
